c: Ironhawks, a minor league hockey team
s: The Ironhawks average 3,400 fans in an arena that holds 7,000. Tickets range from $14 to $48. Corporate suites are full, but family tickets sell poorly, and prices on resale sites are often lower than the box office.
The team president (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend a ticket pricing strategy for next season.
p: Explain factors affecting pricing decisions
Explain the nature and scope of the pricing function
Explain legal considerations for pricing
Explain the nature of sales forecasts
Explain the role of customer service as a component of selling relationships
n: Considers demand, competition and perceived value
Proposes dynamic pricing, family packs or flexible plans
Explains how pricing must follow consumer protection rules
Forecasts attendance and revenue under each option
Keeps loyal ticket holders valued
q: How would your plan affect season ticket holders?
Would you restrict resale prices? Why or why not?

c: Summit Music Festival, a three-day outdoor festival
s: Summit Music Festival's ticket sales are down 15% from last year. Surveys show fans are unhappy with long lines and rising prices, and a new competing festival is taking place the same month.
The festival director (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend a promotional plan to recover sales.
p: Explain the nature of a promotional plan
Identify the elements of the promotional mix
Explain the nature of buzz-marketing
Explain the use of video/images for digital marketing
Describe the use of business ethics in promotion
n: Sets goals for sales and timing
Combines advertising, social media, partnerships and public relations
Creates buzz with announcements, artist content and fan sharing
Uses video from past festivals
Avoids misleading claims about lineup or pricing
q: How would you respond to fans who say the festival is too expensive?
What would you do if the headliner canceled?

c: Metro City FC, a professional soccer club
s: Metro City FC fans say it is hard to buy tickets, parking is confusing and staff do not answer questions. Season ticket renewals fell from 82% to 68%.
The chief operating officer (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how to improve the fan experience and increase renewals.
p: Demonstrate a customer service mindset
Describe the use of technology in customer relationship management
Build and maintain relationships with customers
Handle customer/client complaints
Solicit feedback
n: Treats fans as long-term customers
Improves app, ticketing and communication
Personalizes outreach to season ticket holders
Responds to complaints quickly
Surveys fans and acts on feedback
q: What would you do to win back a season ticket holder who did not renew?

s: Velocity Sports Network streams games to 2 million subscribers. Younger viewers watch highlights on social media instead of full games, and the network struggles to prove the value of advertising to sponsors.
The vice president (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how to gather and use audience information.
p: Apply marketing analytics
Interpret statistical findings
Translate research findings into actionable business recommendations
Explain ethical considerations in providing information
Maintain security of marketing data
n: Tracks viewing time, devices and content preferences
Compares groups and trends
Recommends content and sponsor packages based on data
Protects viewer privacy and is transparent
Secures data and limits access
q: How would you prove to sponsors that social highlights help the network?
What data would you not collect, and why?

s: During a recent concert, a crowd surge caused several minor injuries. Exits were crowded, communication between security and staff was slow, and the arena had no clear plan for sudden weather alerts.
The general manager (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how to improve safety planning and communication.
p: Explain the nature of risk management
Conduct a risk assessment of an event
Handle and report emergency situations
Explain routine security precautions
Coordinate activities with those of other departments
n: Identifies hazards such as crowd flow, weather and exits
Rates likelihood and consequence and plans responses
Creates emergency procedures and drills
Uses trained staff, clear signage and technology
Coordinates security, medical, operations and local agencies
q: What would you do if the artist wanted to continue the show during a severe weather alert?
How would you train part-time staff for emergencies?
